newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suicide attacks allowed only by ruler - Egypt mufti.
newsitem.headline: Suicide attacks allowed only by ruler - Egypt mufti.

text.p: Egypt's highest Moslem religious authority said in an interview published on Saturday that it was allowed in Islam for individuals to launch suicide attacks but only if it was part of their government's policy.
The Mufti, Nasr Farid Mohamed Wasel, was answering a question by the London-based Arabic daily al-Hayat about his position on the legality of suicide attacks in occupied lands.
"Jihad (Holy Struggle) is an issue which imposes itself on current reality, but common interests are more important than individual ones," he was quoted as saying.

"The ruler is the one who draws up a general policy for Jihad's required framework. In this context the suicide operation is permissible provided that individual behaviour is under the umbrella of general policy put into place by the ruler."
Lebanese and Palestinian militants have adopted suicide attacks as a technique in their fight against Israel's occupation of Arab land.

Wasel, an Islamic law professor, was appointed as mufti of Egypt earlier this month. The mufti issues fatwas, or legal opinions, on issues ranging from family life to economic practice. He also gives final approval to death sentences.
He also said that defending Jerusalem's Arab character was a religious duty. "Jerusalem is Arab by history and defending it is a holy duty..the call to globalise it is wrong."
